summary: PLANSX, “The Earth, Decoded.”, is a free web app that turns NASA FIRMS wildfire detections into one clear map and one calendar. The challenge asks us to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS, but the two sensors see fires at different resolutions, about 1 km and 375 m, so their counts cannot be compared directly. We built a transparent method that scales MODIS to the VIIRS level, groups detections into 0.25 degree cells and gives every cell a level from 0 to 10. The five satellites stay separate, and the app shows “not available” when one has no data. Anyone can explore the world by country, period or satellite, see a daily calendar, compare years and download yearly files. It matters because wildfires affect air, climate and communities everywhere, and people need data they can understand, not only experts.
details:
PLANSX is a web app we built with Flutter. You choose a place, a time period and a satellite, and the app shows you where fires were detected. You can see it on a 3D globe or on a flat map, with five different views of the data. There is also a calendar where every day is colored by how much fire activity there was. If you tap a day, you see the details by level and by satellite. Another page shows which years and months had the most hotspots and how the current year compares with the average.

The challenge is to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS. MODIS sees the ground at about 1 km and VIIRS at 375 m, so the numbers cannot be compared directly. We use NASA FIRMS detections with medium and high confidence. We scale MODIS to the VIIRS level using a factor taken from the years when both satellites worked together. Then we group detections into cells of 0.25 degrees, about 28 km, and give each cell a level from 0 to 10. Terra and Aqua stay separate. If a satellite has no data, the app says “not available” and we never fill the gap. This is a statistical scaling and not a physical calibration, and the app says so.

We made it for students, teachers, journalists and communities who want to understand fire activity without special tools. What makes it different is one level scale for all sensors, a calendar that works like a diary of the planet, and a design made for people who are not experts.

We used Flutter and Dart, flutter_map, Python for the NASA data, GitHub and Vercel for publishing. We also used Claude as an AI assistant for coding, debugging, data scripts, text and translations, design, the demo video and its background music. The ideas, the decisions and the voice in the video are ours.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS active fire data)
